documents.name: Biopsy of Oral Tissue
documents.overview: TEST SUCCESSFUL CUSTOMIZATION
documents.originalOverview:
Biopsy of Oral Tissue
 
Purpose: Surgical removal of a small tissue sample from the mouth for diagnosis.
First 24 Hours:
- Bite on gauze for 30–45 minutes to control bleeding.
- Avoid disturbing the site with your tongue or fingers.
- Do not rinse, spit, or use a straw for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild soreness is normal; take OTC or prescribed pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the face for 20 minutes on/off for the first few hours if needed.
Bleeding:
- A small amount of oozing is normal for 1–2 days.
- Apply firm pressure with gauze if bleeding increases.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the biopsy site for several days.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first 1–2 days.
- Avoid hot, spicy, or acidic foods that may irritate the site.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may dissolve on their own or require removal.
- Contact the office if you experience persistent bleeding, increasing pain, or swelling after day 3.

documents.name: Amalgam Fillings
documents.overview:
What Was Done:
You received amalgam (silver) filling(s) today. These restorations are designed to restore the full function and structure of your teeth.

Immediate Post-Treatment (First 4 Hours):
• Avoid chewing on the treated side until numbness completely wears off
• Do not eat or drink anything hot for the first 2 hours
• Avoid hard, sticky, or chewy foods that could dislodge or damage the new filling

First 24 Hours - The Critical Period:
• Remember, IT CAN TAKE 24 HOURS FOR THE FILLING TO FULLY HARDEN! So be gentle.....
• Some sensitivity to temperature and pressure is normal and should gradually decrease
• Continue to chew carefully, preferably on the opposite side
• Avoid very hot or very cold foods and beverages
• Take over-the-counter pain medication as needed (follow package directions)

Managing Sensitivity:
• Mild sensitivity to cold, heat, or pressure may persist for several days to weeks
• Use toothpaste designed for sensitive teeth if needed
• If sensitivity increases or persists beyond 2 weeks, contact our office

Bite Adjustment:
• Your bite may feel different initially - this is normal
• If the filling feels "high" or your bite feels uneven after 24-48 hours, call for a bite adjustment
• Do not attempt to adjust the filling yourself by excessive chewing or grinding

Long-Term Care:
• Resume normal oral hygiene after 24 hours
• Brush gently around the new filling
• Floss carefully to avoid dislodging the restoration
• Regular dental checkups are important to monitor the filling

When to Call:
• Severe or worsening pain after 48 hours
• Sharp edges that irritate your tongue or cheek
• If the filling feels loose or falls out
• Signs of infection (fever, severe swelling, persistent bad taste)
• Bite problems that don't resolve after 2-3 days

Your amalgam filling should provide many years of service with proper care. Contact our office if you have any concerns.

documents.name: Alveoloplasty
documents.overview:
Purpose:
Alveoloplasty involves reshaping the jaw bone to create a smooth, even surface for optimal healing and future prosthetic placement.

First 24–48 Hours:
• Apply ice packs to the outside of your face for 15-20 minutes on, 10 minutes off during the first 24 hours
• Keep your head elevated when lying down to minimize swelling
• Avoid rinsing, spitting, or using straws for the first 24 hours
• Take prescribed pain medication as directed
• Rest and limit physical activity

Pain & Sensitivity:
• Some discomfort is normal and expected after this procedure
• Peak discomfort typically occurs 2-3 days after surgery
• Take prescribed pain medication as directed, or use over-the-counter medications as recommended
• Contact us if pain increases significantly after the third day

Oral Hygiene:
• Do not brush or floss near the surgical site for the first 24 hours
• Beginning the second day, gently rinse with warm salt water (1/2 teaspoon salt in 8 oz warm water)
• Brush other teeth normally, avoiding the surgical area
• After one week, gentle brushing of the area may be resumed

Diet:
• Soft, cool foods for the first 48 hours (yogurt, smoothies, soup, mashed potatoes)
• Avoid hot foods and beverages for the first 24 hours
• Gradually return to normal diet as comfort allows
• Stay well hydrated
• Avoid alcohol and tobacco products during healing

Special Precautions:
• Do not smoke or use tobacco products - this significantly impairs healing
• Avoid vigorous rinsing or spitting
• Do not probe the area with your tongue or fingers
• Follow all post-operative medication instructions
• Attend all scheduled follow-up appointments

Follow-Up:
• Return for suture removal if non-dissolving stitches were placed
• Contact our office if you experience excessive bleeding, severe pain, or signs of infection
• Complete healing typically takes 2-4 weeks
• Future prosthetic planning will be discussed at follow-up appointments

documents.name: Apicoectomy
documents.overview:
Apicoectomy
 
Purpose: Surgical removal of the tip of a tooth root and surrounding infected tissue, often after a root canal.
First 24 Hours:
- Keep the surgical area clean and avoid disturbing it.
- Use gauze to control bleeding as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the face for 20 minutes on/off for the first 6–8 hours.
Pain & Swelling:
- Take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as needed.
- Swelling and minor bruising may occur and peak at 48–72 hours.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing the surgical site for several days.
- Use any prescribed antimicrobial rinse as directed.
- Brush remaining teeth normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first few days.
- Avoid chewing on the affected side until cleared by your dentist.
Activity:
- Limit strenuous activity for 48 hours.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may be removed after about 1 week.
- Contact the office if pain worsens, swelling increases after day 3, or you notice signs of infection.

documents.name: Biopsy Oral Soft Tissue
documents.overview:
Biopsy (Oral Soft Tissue)
 
Purpose: Removal of a small tissue sample from the mouth for laboratory examination.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours to protect the clot.
- Apply an ice pack externally in 15-minute intervals to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Some mild discomfort when chewing or speaking is normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth gently, avoiding the biopsy site for the first few days.
- Rinse with warm salt water starting 24 hours after the procedure to promote healing.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first 48 hours.
- Avoid spicy, acidic, or crunchy foods that may irritate the area.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid touching or pulling on the biopsy site with your tongue or fingers.
- If stitches are placed, follow instructions for care and removal.
Follow-Up:
- Biopsy results are typically available within 1–2 weeks.
- Contact the office if there is excessive bleeding, severe pain, or signs of infection.

documents.name: Bone Grafting Implant Site
documents.overview:
Bone Grafting for Implant Site Development
 
Purpose: Placement of bone graft material to increase bone volume and quality in preparation for future dental
implant placement.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for 24 hours to protect the graft.
- Apply an ice pack externally in 15-minute intervals to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Some soreness in the jaw and chewing muscles is normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth carefully, avoiding the graft site for the first few days.
- Rinse gently with warm salt water starting 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first 48–72 hours.
- Avoid chewing directly on the graft site.
Special Precautions:
- Do not disturb the graft area with your tongue, fingers, or dental tools.
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they can delay healing.
- Follow all instructions regarding antibiotics or mouth rinses.
Follow-Up:
- Sutures may dissolve on their own or require removal.
- Contact the office if graft material becomes exposed, excessive bleeding occurs, or signs of infection appear.

documents.name: Bone Grafting Ridge Preservation
documents.overview:
Bone Grafting for Ridge Preservation (After Extraction)
Purpose: Placement of bone graft material in the socket after tooth extraction to preserve bone height and width
for future restorative treatment.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for 24 hours to protect the graft.
- Apply an ice pack externally in 15-minute intervals to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Some soreness when chewing or speaking is normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth carefully, avoiding the graft site for the first few days.
- Rinse gently with warm salt water starting 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first 48 hours.
- Avoid chewing directly on the graft site.
Special Precautions:
- Do not disturb the graft material with your tongue or fingers.
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they can impair healing.
Follow-Up:
- Sutures may dissolve on their own or require removal, depending on the type used.
- Contact the office if you notice graft material dislodging, excessive bleeding, or signs of infection.

documents.name: Bone Grafting
documents.overview:
Bone Grafting
 
Purpose: Placement of bone or bone substitute to build up jawbone for future dental implants.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid disturbing the graft site with your tongue, fingers, or food.
- Do not rinse, spit, or use a straw.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild to moderate discomfort is normal; take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the cheek for 20 minutes on/off for the first 6–8 hours.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or pink saliva is normal for 24–48 hours.
- Apply firm pressure with gauze if bleeding increases.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the graft site for 1 week.
- Use antimicrobial mouth rinse if prescribed.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for several days.
- Avoid seeds, nuts, chips, or foods that could get lodged in the surgical site.
Follow-Up:
- Graft material may appear as small granules in the mouth — this is normal early in healing.
- Contact the office if you experience increasing pain, swelling, or discharge from the site.

documents.name: Cleft Lip Palate Repair
documents.overview:
Cleft Lip and/or Palate Repair
 
Purpose: Surgical correction of a congenital split in the lip and/or roof of the mouth to improve appearance,
speech, feeding, and overall function.
First 24–72 Hours:
- Swelling, mild bleeding, and discomfort are expected.
- Apply ice packs externally (if advised) to reduce swelling.
- Keep the head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Give prescribed pain medication and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Mild irritability or feeding difficulties may occur in infants.
Oral Hygiene:
- Follow your surgeon’s instructions for cleaning the surgical area.
- Use gentle rinses if prescribed; avoid brushing directly on sutures.
Diet:
- Infants may require specialized bottles or feeding techniques.
- Older children and adults should follow a soft or liquid diet as instructed.
Special Precautions:
- Prevent the child from putting fingers, toys, or other objects in the mouth.
- Use arm restraints if recommended to avoid touching the surgical site.
- Avoid strenuous activity until cleared by your surgeon.
Follow-Up:
- Multiple follow-up appointments are needed to monitor healing and speech development.
- Contact your surgeon if there is persistent bleeding, fever, swelling after 3 days, or feeding refusal.

documents.name: Connective Tissue Graft
documents.overview:
Connective Tissue Graft
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure in which connective tissue is taken from under the surface of the palate and placed
over an exposed tooth root to treat gum recession.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort at both the donor and graft sites are common.
- Apply ice packs for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Mild sensitivity to hot, cold, or pressure is normal for several weeks.
Oral Hygiene:
- Do not brush or floss near the graft site until instructed by your dentist.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to maintain cleanliness.
Diet:
- Eat only soft foods for at least 1 week.
- Avoid hot, spicy, crunchy, or sticky foods.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid stretching your lip or cheek to look at the graft.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up appointments to assess graft success.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Crown Lengthening with Bone Removal
documents.overview:
Crown Lengthening with Bone Removal
 
Purpose: A surgical procedure to expose more of a tooth's structure by reshaping the gum tissue and removing
some underlying bone, often for restorative or cosmetic purposes.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are normal.
- Apply ice packs for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated when resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Mild tooth sensitivity may persist for several weeks.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the surgical site for the first week.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to keep the area clean.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for the first 3–5 days.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or spicy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid strenuous physical activity for 48 hours.
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend all scheduled follow-up appointments for suture removal and healing checks.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding continues, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Crown Lengthening
documents.overview:
Crown Lengthening
 
Purpose: Reshaping gum tissue and bone to expose more of the tooth structure for restorative or cosmetic
purposes.
First 24 Hours:
- Keep gauze in place for 30–45 minutes to control bleeding.
- Avoid rinsing, spitting, or using a straw.
- Keep head elevated when resting.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild to moderate discomfort is normal; take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the face for 20 minutes on/off for the first 6–8 hours.
Bleeding:
- Light bleeding or pink saliva may occur for 1–2 days.
- Apply gentle pressure with gauze if bleeding increases.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing the surgical site for 1–2 weeks or as directed.
- Use antimicrobial mouth rinse if prescribed.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for several days.
- Avoid spicy, crunchy, or hot foods that could irritate the surgical site.
Special Precautions:
- Limit physical activity for 48 hours.
- Do not smoke, as it delays healing.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may dissolve or be removed in 1–2 weeks.
- Contact the office if swelling worsens, pain increases, or bleeding persists beyond 48 hours.

documents.name: Dental Bonding
documents.overview:
Dental Bonding
 
Purpose: Application of tooth-colored composite resin to repair chips, cracks, discoloration, or gaps.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing until numbness wears off.
- Composite resin is fully set when you leave the office, but be gentle for the rest of the day.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild sensitivity to temperature may occur for a few days.
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally.
- Avoid abrasive toothpaste that may scratch the resin.
Diet:
- Avoid very hard or sticky foods for the first 24 hours.
- Limit staining foods and drinks to prevent discoloration.
Special Precautions:
- Do not use teeth as tools to open packages or bite hard objects.
- Bonding material can chip—avoid nail-biting or chewing on pens.
Follow-Up:
- Bonding may last several years but can stain or wear over time.
- Contact the office if you notice chips, cracks, or roughness.

documents.name: Dental Bridge Placement
documents.overview:
Dental Bridge Placement
 
Purpose: Replacement of one or more missing teeth using a fixed bridge anchored to adjacent teeth.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing on the bridge until numbness wears off.
- Temporary bridges require extra care; avoid sticky or hard foods until permanent bridge is placed.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild soreness or temperature sensitivity is normal.
- Use OTC pain relievers as needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush normally but use a floss threader or special cleaning aid to clean under the bridge.
- Be gentle around temporary bridges.
Diet:
- Avoid very hard, sticky, or chewy foods if you have a temporary bridge.
- After permanent bridge placement, resume normal diet as comfort allows.
Special Precautions:
- If your bite feels uneven after numbness wears off, contact the office for adjustment.
- If a temporary bridge comes off, replace it with temporary dental cement and call the office.
Follow-Up:
- Permanent bridges should feel comfortable and natural.
- Contact the office if pain worsens, swelling occurs, or the bridge feels loose.

documents.name: Dental Crown Placement
documents.overview:
Dental Crown Placement
 
Purpose: Covering and protecting a damaged or weakened tooth with a custom-made cap.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing on the crowned tooth until numbness wears off.
- Temporary crowns require extra care; avoid sticky or hard foods until permanent crown is placed.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild soreness or temperature sensitivity is normal.
- Use OTC pain relievers as needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, but slide floss out rather than pulling up to avoid dislodging a temporary crown.
Diet:
- Avoid very hard, sticky, or chewy foods if you have a temporary crown.
- After permanent crown placement, resume normal diet as comfort allows.
Special Precautions:
- If your bite feels uneven after numbness wears off, contact the office for adjustment.
- If a temporary crown comes off, replace it with temporary dental cement and call the office.
Follow-Up:
- Permanent crowns should feel comfortable and natural.
- Contact the office if pain worsens, swelling occurs, or the crown feels loose.

documents.name: Dental Implant Placement
documents.overview:
Dental Implant Placement
 
Purpose: Surgical placement of a titanium post into the jawbone to replace a missing tooth.
First 24 Hours:
- Bite on gauze for 30–45 minutes to control bleeding.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using a straw to protect the blood clot.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Swelling:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain medication as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the cheek for 20 minutes on/off for the first 6–8 hours.
- Swelling and minor bruising may occur and peak at 48–72 hours.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or pink saliva is normal for 24–48 hours.
- Apply firm pressure with gauze if bleeding increases.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing the surgical site for several days.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial mouth rinse if provided.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for several days.
- Avoid chewing on the implant site.
Activity:
- Avoid strenuous activity for 48 hours.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may dissolve or require removal after 1 week.
- Report persistent pain, swelling, or loosening of the implant immediately.

documents.name: Dental Sealants
documents.overview:
Dental Sealants
 
Purpose: Thin protective coatings applied to the chewing surfaces of back teeth to help prevent decay.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing until numbness wears off if anesthesia was used.
- Sealants harden immediately, so normal eating can resume right away unless told otherwise.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Sealants are usually painless; mild gum tenderness may occur if soft tissue was touched.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally.
- Sealants protect the tooth surface but do not replace good oral hygiene.
Diet:
- Avoid chewing very hard foods (ice, hard candy) that could chip the sealant.
- Sticky foods may loosen sealants over time.
Special Precautions:
- If you feel roughness or a sealant seems loose, contact the office for evaluation.
Follow-Up:
- Sealants can last several years but should be checked regularly at dental visits.
- Touch-ups may be needed to maintain full protection.

documents.name: Denture Delivery
documents.overview:
Denture Delivery (Full and Partial)
 
Purpose: Replacement of missing teeth with removable full or partial dentures.
First 24 Hours:
- Wear dentures as instructed, often for the first 24 hours continuously to help your mouth adjust.
- Minor soreness or pressure spots are normal.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed.
- Warm salt water rinses can help relieve sore spots.
Oral Hygiene:
- Remove dentures daily for cleaning using a denture brush and cleanser.
- Clean gums, tongue, and any remaining teeth with a soft brush.
Diet:
- Start with soft foods cut into small pieces.
- Chew slowly using both sides of your mouth.
Special Precautions:
- Do not attempt to adjust dentures yourself; this may cause damage.
- Keep dentures moist when not in use to prevent warping.
Follow-Up:
- Expect adjustment appointments to relieve sore spots and improve fit.
- Contact the office if discomfort persists or dentures feel loose.

documents.name: Denture Reline
documents.overview:
Denture Reline
 
Purpose: Adjustment of the inner surface of a denture to improve fit and comfort.
First 24 Hours:
- Wear dentures as instructed, typically for the first 24 hours continuously to help adapt to the new fit.
- Some minor soreness or pressure spots are normal.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed.
- Warm salt water rinses can soothe irritated gums.
Oral Hygiene:
- Remove dentures daily for cleaning using a denture brush and cleanser.
- Clean gums, tongue, and any remaining teeth with a soft brush.
Diet:
- Start with soft foods and gradually reintroduce firmer foods as comfort improves.
- Chew evenly on both sides.
Special Precautions:
- Do not attempt to adjust dentures yourself.
- Keep dentures moist when not in use to prevent warping.
Follow-Up:
- Adjustments may be needed to fine-tune the fit.
- Contact the office if discomfort persists or dentures feel unstable.

documents.name: Free Gingival Graft
documents.overview:
Free Gingival Graft
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure where a piece of gum tissue is taken from one area (usually the palate) and placed
on another area to increase gum thickness or cover exposed roots.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are common.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Expect mild discomfort at both the donor and recipient sites.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing or flossing near the graft site until advised.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to keep the area clean.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for at least 1 week.
- Avoid hot, spicy, crunchy, or hard foods that may irritate the graft.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid pulling on the lip or cheek to look at the graft.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled follow-up visits to monitor graft healing.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Frenectomy
documents.overview:
Frenectomy
 
Purpose: Removal or reshaping of a frenum (small fold of tissue) to improve function or fit of dentures.
First 24 Hours:
- Keep gauze in place for 30–45 minutes to control bleeding.
- Avoid excessive talking or movement of the lips to prevent tension on the site.
Pain & Swelling:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as needed.
- Apply ice packs to the face in 20-minute intervals for the first few hours.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or pink saliva may occur for 1–2 days.
- Apply gentle pressure with gauze if needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the surgical site for 1 week.
- Begin gentle warm saltwater rinses after 24 hours.
Diet:
- Soft, cool foods for the first 2–3 days.
- Avoid acidic foods that may sting.
Follow-Up:
- Suture removal if required.
- Call if swelling worsens, pain increases, or bleeding persists.

documents.name: Full Mouth Rehabilitation
documents.overview:
Full Mouth Rehabilitation (Multiple Restorations)
 
Purpose: Comprehensive treatment involving multiple crowns, bridges, implants, or other restorations to restore
function, aesthetics, and oral health.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild soreness in teeth, gums, and jaw is normal.
- Avoid chewing hard foods until bite is fully adjusted.
- Some temperature sensitivity may occur temporarily.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take OTC pain relievers as needed.
- Sensitivity toothpaste can help with cold or heat sensitivity.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush twice daily with a soft-bristled toothbrush.
- Floss daily, using floss threaders or interdental brushes where needed.
- Avoid overly abrasive toothpaste to protect new restorations.
Diet:
- Soft diet for the first 24–48 hours, gradually resuming normal foods.
- Avoid sticky, hard, or overly chewy foods that could damage restorations.
Special Precautions:
- If temporary restorations are present, avoid biting into hard foods until permanent ones are placed.
- Report any bite discomfort to your dentist for adjustment.
Follow-Up:
- Attend all scheduled follow-up appointments to ensure proper fit and function.
- Contact the office if restorations feel loose, crack, or cause persistent discomfort.

documents.name: Gingivectomy Gingivoplasty
documents.overview:
Gingivectomy / Gingivoplasty
 
Purpose: Surgical removal (gingivectomy) or reshaping (gingivoplasty) of gum tissue to treat disease or improve
aesthetics.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Apply ice packs externally in 15-minute intervals for swelling control.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Tooth sensitivity and gum tenderness are normal during healing.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush gently around the surgical site with a soft-bristled toothbrush.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses as directed.
- Avoid flossing in the treated area until advised.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first few days.
- Avoid hot, spicy, acidic, or crunchy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Do not pull on the lips or cheeks to inspect the site.
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they delay healing.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches (if placed) may dissolve or require removal.
- Contact the office if excessive bleeding, severe pain, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Gingivectomy
documents.overview:
Gingivectomy
 
Purpose: Surgical removal of excess gum tissue to treat gum disease or improve aesthetics.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid disturbing the surgical area.
- Do not rinse, spit, or use a straw.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild discomfort and swelling are normal.
- Take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the cheek for 20 minutes on/off for the first 4–6 hours.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or pink saliva is normal for 1–2 days.
- Apply gentle pressure with gauze if bleeding increases.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing the surgical site for 1–2 weeks or until cleared by your dentist.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinse if provided.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for several days.
- Avoid spicy, crunchy, or hot foods that could irritate healing tissue.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may dissolve or require removal in 1–2 weeks.
- Contact the office if swelling worsens, pain increases, or bleeding persists beyond 48 hours.

documents.name: Guided Tissue Regeneration
documents.overview:
Guided Tissue Regeneration
 
Purpose: A periodontal procedure that uses a barrier membrane to direct the growth of new bone and gum tissue
where it has been lost.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep your head elevated when resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics as directed.
- Mild sensitivity to hot and cold may persist for several weeks.
Oral Hygiene:
- Do not brush or floss near the surgical site until instructed by your dentist.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to keep the area clean.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for the first 3–5 days.
- Avoid chewing on the treated side, and avoid spicy, hard, or crunchy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol during healing.
- Do not disturb the surgical site with your tongue or fingers.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up visits to ensure proper healing and membrane stability.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection develop.

documents.name: Gum Contouring Gingivoplasty
documents.overview:
Gum Contouring (Gingivoplasty)
 
Purpose: Cosmetic procedure to reshape the gum line for improved appearance, often performed with a laser or
scalpel.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild swelling, tenderness, and minor bleeding are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first few hours.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take over-the-counter or prescribed pain medications as directed.
- Mild sensitivity to temperature changes is common.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly on treated gums for the first few days.
- Use prescribed mouth rinses to keep the area clean.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first 48 hours.
- Avoid spicy, acidic, or crunchy foods until healing progresses.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol during healing.
- Do not pull on the lips or cheeks to view the gums.
Follow-Up:
- Attend any scheduled follow-up visits to monitor healing.
- Contact your dentist if swelling worsens after 3 days, bleeding persists, or you notice signs of infection.

documents.name: Hemisection Root Resection
documents.overview:
Hemisection or Root Resection of Multi-Rooted Teeth
Purpose: Surgical removal of one root (root resection) or one half of a multi-rooted tooth (hemisection) to
preserve the remaining structure.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Apply ice packs externally in 15-minute intervals to reduce swelling.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Sensitivity in the treated tooth and gums is common.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush gently around the surgical site with a soft-bristled toothbrush.
- Begin warm salt water rinses after 24 hours, several times daily.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for the first few days.
- Avoid chewing on the treated side.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they can delay healing.
- Follow all restorative instructions if a crown or filling will be placed later.
Follow-Up:
- Sutures may dissolve or require removal.
- Contact the office if swelling worsens after 3 days, bleeding is excessive, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Hemisection
documents.overview:
Hemisection
 
Purpose: Surgical removal of one root and the overlying portion of a multi-rooted tooth, often to preserve the
remaining healthy tooth structure.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Tooth sensitivity and gum tenderness may last for several days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth gently, avoiding the surgical site for the first few days.
- Begin gentle warm salt water rinses 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Soft foods for at least 48 hours.
- Avoid chewing on the treated side until cleared by your dentist.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol during healing.
- Do not disturb the surgical site with your tongue or fingers.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled follow-up visits to assess healing and tooth stability.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Immediate Dentures
documents.overview:
Immediate Dentures
 
Purpose: Dentures placed immediately after tooth extraction to restore appearance and function.
First 24 Hours:
- Keep dentures in place for the first 24 hours unless instructed otherwise; this helps control swelling and
bleeding.
- Minor soreness, swelling, and difficulty speaking or chewing are normal.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply cold compresses externally to reduce swelling.
Oral Hygiene:
- Rinse gently with warm salt water starting 24 hours after surgery.
- Clean dentures daily with a denture brush and cleanser.
- Clean gums and tongue gently with a soft brush or gauze.
Diet:
- Start with soft, cool foods.
- Avoid very hot, spicy, or hard foods during initial healing.
Special Precautions:
- Do not attempt to adjust dentures yourself; this may cause damage.
- Expect changes in fit as swelling decreases; relining may be required.
Follow-Up:
- Adjustment appointments are necessary to ensure comfort.
- Contact the office if bleeding persists, pain worsens, or dentures feel too loose.

documents.name: Inlays and Onlays
documents.overview:
Inlays and Onlays
 
Purpose: Custom-made restorations used to repair damaged or decayed teeth when a full crown is not needed.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing on the treated tooth until numbness wears off.
- Temporary inlays/onlays require extra care; avoid sticky or hard foods until the permanent restoration is placed.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild sensitivity to temperature or pressure is normal for a few days.
- Use OTC pain relievers as needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, being gentle around temporary restorations.
- Avoid abrasive toothpaste that could scratch surfaces.
Diet:
- Avoid very hard or sticky foods that may dislodge a temporary restoration.
- Resume normal diet after the permanent inlay/onlay is placed.
Special Precautions:
- If your bite feels uneven after numbness wears off, contact the office for adjustment.
- If a temporary inlay/onlay comes loose, replace it with temporary dental cement and call the office.
Follow-Up:
- Permanent inlays/onlays should feel comfortable and natural.
- Contact the office if pain worsens, swelling occurs, or the restoration feels loose.

documents.name: Maxillofacial Trauma Surgery
documents.overview:
Maxillofacial Trauma Surgery
 
Purpose: Surgical repair of facial fractures, jaw injuries, or severe soft tissue damage caused by trauma.
First 24–72 Hours:
- Swelling, bruising, and discomfort are common.
- Apply ice packs to the affected area for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first 24 hours.
- Keep head elevated while resting to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain relievers and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Avoid aspirin unless recommended, as it may increase bleeding risk.
Oral Hygiene:
- Follow your surgeon’s instructions for oral care; often includes gentle antimicrobial rinses.
- Avoid brushing near sutured areas until cleared.
Diet:
- Soft or liquid diet as directed, avoiding chewing on the injured side.
- Avoid hot, spicy, or crunchy foods that could irritate healing tissue.
Special Precautions:
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol during recovery.
- Avoid strenuous activities and contact sports until cleared by your surgeon.
- If jaw fixation (wiring) is used, keep wire cutters or scissors nearby in case of emergency.
Follow-Up:
- Multiple follow-up appointments will be necessary to monitor bone and soft tissue healing.
- Contact your surgeon immediately if you experience persistent bleeding, difficulty breathing, fever, or sudden
changes in bite alignment.

documents.name: Multiple Extractions
documents.overview:
Multiple Extractions
 
Purpose: Removal of several teeth in one visit.
First 24 Hours:
- Follow clot protection steps as with single extractions.
- Expect more swelling and soreness than with one extraction.
- Keep head elevated when resting.
Pain & Swelling:
- Take prescribed pain medication as directed.
- Apply ice packs for 20 minutes on/off during the first 24 hours.
- Swelling may last longer than single extraction cases.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or oozing is normal for the first day.
- Replace gauze and bite with firm pressure for 30 minutes if needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid rinsing for the first 24 hours.
- After 24 hours, gently rinse with warm salt water 3–4 times daily.
- Brush remaining teeth carefully.
Diet:
- Very soft diet for the first 2–3 days.
- Avoid crunchy, hard, or spicy foods until comfortable.
Special Precautions:
- If dentures were placed immediately, do not remove them until instructed by your dentist.
Follow-Up:
- A post-op check may be advised within 24–48 hours to monitor healing.
- Call if swelling increases after day 3, pain worsens, or heavy bleeding continues.

documents.name: Occlusal Guard Nightguard
documents.overview:
Occlusal Guard / Nightguard Delivery
 
Purpose: Custom appliance worn over the teeth to protect against grinding, clenching, or jaw disorders.
First 24 Hours:
- Wear the guard as instructed, usually at night or during specific times of day.
- Some initial tightness or mild discomfort is normal.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild tooth or jaw soreness may occur during the first few days.
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Rinse the guard with cool water after each use.
- Brush it gently with a toothbrush and non-abrasive toothpaste or mild soap.
- Store in a ventilated case when not in use.
Diet:
- Do not eat or drink (except water) while wearing the guard.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid exposing the guard to hot water, which can warp it.
- Keep away from pets, as they may chew on it.
Follow-Up:
- Bring the guard to dental visits for evaluation and cleaning.
- Contact the office if the guard becomes loose, cracked, or uncomfortable.

documents.name: Odontoplasty
documents.overview:
Odontoplasty (Tooth Reshaping)
 
Purpose: Conservative reshaping of tooth enamel to improve appearance, correct bite interferences, or prepare
for other dental procedures.
First 24 Hours:
- Minimal discomfort is expected.
- Mild sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods may occur temporarily.
- No swelling or bleeding should occur.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Sensitivity can be managed with desensitizing toothpaste.
- OTC pain relievers can be used if necessary.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss as normal, using gentle technique.
- Avoid extremely abrasive toothpaste for the first week.
Diet:
- No dietary restrictions are typically needed.
- Avoid extremely hot or cold foods if sensitivity is present.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid biting hard objects (ice, pens) to prevent enamel fracture.
- In cases where bonding was placed after reshaping, avoid staining foods for 48 hours.
Follow-Up:
- Schedule regular dental checkups to monitor the reshaped teeth.
- Contact the office if sensitivity worsens or chips/cracks occur.

documents.name: Oral Biopsy
documents.overview:
Oral Biopsy
 
Purpose: Removal of a small sample of oral tissue for laboratory examination to diagnose abnormalities.
First 24 Hours:
- Minor bleeding and mild discomfort are normal.
- Apply gentle pressure with gauze to control bleeding.
- Keep the head elevated when resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed or OTC pain medication as directed.
- Sensitivity in the area is common for a few days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush carefully, avoiding the biopsy site for the first day.
- Rinse gently with warm salt water starting 24 hours after the procedure.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first day.
- Avoid spicy, acidic, or crunchy foods that may irritate the site.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol until healing is complete.
- Do not disturb the site with your tongue or fingers.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up visits to review biopsy results and further treatment if needed.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection appear.

documents.name: Oral Cancer Screening FollowUp
documents.overview:
Oral Cancer Screening Follow-Up
 
Purpose: Monitoring and follow-up after an oral cancer screening, particularly if an abnormal finding was noted.
First 24 Hours:
- No special restrictions unless a biopsy was performed (follow biopsy instructions if applicable).
- You may resume normal activities immediately.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Typically, no discomfort occurs after a standard screening.
- If tissue sampling or scraping was done, mild soreness may occur.
Oral Hygiene:
- Continue normal brushing and flossing.
- Avoid irritating any areas of the mouth that feel sensitive.
Diet:
- No restrictions unless otherwise advised.
Special Precautions:
- Monitor any areas identified by your dentist for changes in size, color, or sensation.
- Avoid tobacco and limit alcohol, as they increase cancer risk.
Follow-Up:
- Follow the recommended re-examination schedule (often every 6–12 months).
- Contact the office immediately if you notice lumps, persistent sores, white or red patches, or unexplained oral
pain.

documents.name: Oral Cancer Surgery
documents.overview:
Oral Cancer Surgery
 
Purpose: Surgical removal of malignant tumors from the mouth, tongue, jaw, or surrounding tissues, often
followed by reconstruction.
First 24–72 Hours:
- Swelling, bruising, and discomfort are common.
- Apply ice packs for the first 24 hours to reduce swelling.
- Keep the head elevated to minimize swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Numbness or changes in speech/swallowing may occur, depending on surgical site.
Oral Hygiene:
- Follow your surgeon’s instructions for gentle cleaning of the surgical area.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to reduce infection risk.
Diet:
- Soft or liquid diet as recommended, possibly requiring a feeding tube in extensive surgeries.
- Avoid hot, spicy, or acidic foods that may irritate the site.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they delay healing and increase cancer recurrence risk.
- Speech or swallowing therapy may be needed as part of recovery.
Follow-Up:
- Multiple follow-up visits will be scheduled to monitor healing and check for recurrence.
- Contact your surgeon immediately if you notice persistent bleeding, swelling after 3 days, fever, or difficulty
breathing.

documents.name: Oral Lesion Removal
documents.overview:
Oral Lesion Removal
 
Purpose: Surgical excision of benign or suspicious growths, ulcers, or lesions from the oral cavity.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Apply gauze with gentle pressure if bleeding occurs.
- Keep the head elevated to minimize swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take OTC or prescribed pain relievers as directed.
- Some tenderness in the area is common for several days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth carefully, avoiding direct contact with the surgical site.
- Begin gentle warm salt water rinses 24 hours after the procedure.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first 1–2 days.
- Avoid spicy, acidic, and crunchy foods until the area heals.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they delay healing.
- Do not disturb the site with your tongue or fingers.
Follow-Up:
- Return for follow-up as scheduled to check healing and review pathology results if applicable.
- Contact the office if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection develop.

documents.name: Orthodontic Adjustment
documents.overview:
Orthodontic Adjustment
 
Purpose: Routine tightening or activation of braces to continue tooth movement.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild soreness or pressure on teeth is common.
- Avoid very hard or sticky foods during this time.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers as needed for discomfort.
- Warm salt water rinses can soothe irritated gums or cheeks.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush thoroughly after every meal using an orthodontic toothbrush.
- Floss with a floss threader or use interdental brushes.
Diet:
- Avoid hard, sticky, or chewy foods that can damage braces.
- Stick to softer foods if teeth are sore.
Special Precautions:
- Use orthodontic wax to cover any brackets or wires causing irritation.
- Contact the office if a wire or bracket breaks or becomes loose.
Follow-Up:
- Adjustments are typically needed every 4–8 weeks.
- Good home care is essential to prevent decalcification and cavities.

documents.name: Orthodontic Appliance Delivery
documents.overview:
Orthodontic Appliance Delivery (Expanders, Retainers, etc.)
Purpose: Placement of a custom appliance to aid in orthodontic treatment or retention.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild soreness or pressure is normal as you adjust to the appliance.
- Speech changes or increased saliva production may occur temporarily.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed for discomfort.
- Warm salt water rinses can help with soft tissue irritation.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss carefully around the appliance.
- For removable appliances, clean daily with a toothbrush and mild soap or appliance cleaner.
- Avoid hot water, which can warp plastic components.
Diet:
- Avoid hard, sticky, or chewy foods that could damage the appliance.
- Cut food into smaller pieces for easier chewing.
Special Precautions:
- Wear the appliance as directed to ensure treatment success.
- Store removable appliances in a protective case when not in use.
- Keep away from pets, as they may chew on them.
Follow-Up:
- Bring the appliance to all adjustment or check-up appointments.
- Contact the office if the appliance becomes loose, damaged, or causes sores.

documents.name: Orthognathic Lower Jaw
documents.overview:
Orthognathic Surgery: Lower Jaw (Mandibular Osteotomy)
Purpose: Surgical repositioning of the lower jaw to correct functional or aesthetic issues such as bite problems,
asymmetry, or sleep apnea.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Swelling and bruising will be significant; peak swelling usually occurs within 48–72 hours.
- Apply ice packs externally in 20-minute intervals for the first 48 hours.
- Keep head elevated when resting to reduce swelling.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws during the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications on schedule.
- Numbness in the lips, chin, or tongue is common and may be temporary or permanent.
Oral Hygiene:
- Use a prescribed antimicrobial rinse as directed.
- Gently brush teeth with a soft toothbrush, avoiding surgical areas.
- Irrigation syringes may be provided to clean food from the surgical site.
Diet:
- Follow a liquid or pureed diet as recommended by your surgeon.
- Avoid chewing until cleared by your provider.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid strenuous activity for at least 2 weeks.
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol during healing.
- Rubber bands or fixation devices may be in place; follow all instructions.
Follow-Up:
- Attend all post-op visits for monitoring and adjustments.
- Contact the office if there is sudden swelling, high fever, difficulty breathing, or signs of infection.

documents.name: Orthognathic Surgery
documents.overview:
Orthognathic Surgery (Jaw Surgery)
 
Purpose: Corrective jaw surgery to align the jaws and teeth, often to improve function, bite, and appearance.
First 48–72 Hours:
- Significant swelling, bruising, and mild bleeding are normal.
- Apply ice packs for 20 minutes at a time during the first 24–48 hours.
- Keep your head elevated, even while sleeping.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications, antibiotics, and anti-inflammatory drugs as directed.
- Some numbness or tingling in the lips, cheeks, or tongue is common and may take weeks to resolve.
Oral Hygiene:
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses instead of brushing near the surgical area during the first week.
- After clearance from your surgeon, gently brush using a soft-bristled toothbrush.
Diet:
- Liquid or pureed diet for the first few weeks.
- Gradually transition to soft foods as directed by your surgeon.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid strenuous activities for at least 2 weeks.
- Follow any elastic band or splint instructions carefully.
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Regular follow-up visits will be scheduled to monitor healing and jaw function.
- Contact your surgeon if swelling worsens after 3 days, you have persistent bleeding, fever, or difficulty
breathing.

documents.name: Orthognathic Upper Jaw
documents.overview:
Orthognathic Surgery: Upper Jaw (Maxillary Osteotomy)
Purpose: Surgical repositioning of the upper jaw to correct bite problems, facial asymmetry, or airway issues.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Swelling and bruising will be significant, peaking at 48–72 hours.
- Apply ice packs externally for 20 minutes at a time during the first 48 hours.
- Keep your head elevated when resting to minimize swelling.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications as directed.
- Temporary numbness or tingling in the cheeks, lips, or nose is common.
Oral Hygiene:
- Use a prescribed antimicrobial rinse as directed.
- Brush teeth gently with a soft toothbrush, avoiding surgical sites.
- An irrigation syringe may be provided to keep the surgical area clean.
Diet:
- Follow a liquid or pureed diet for the initial healing phase.
- Do not chew until your surgeon gives clearance.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid strenuous activity for at least 2 weeks.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol while healing.
- Elastic bands or fixation devices may be used; follow instructions carefully.
Follow-Up:
- Attend all post-op appointments for monitoring and adjustments.
- Call the office if you experience sudden swelling, high fever, difficulty breathing, or signs of infection.

documents.name: Osseous Surgery
documents.overview:
Osseous Surgery
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure to reshape or remove diseased bone around teeth to reduce periodontal pockets
and improve gum health.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated to minimize swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Mild tooth sensitivity, especially to temperature, may occur for several weeks.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the surgical site for the first week.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to keep the mouth clean.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first 3–5 days.
- Avoid spicy, acidic, hard, or crunchy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid strenuous activities for 48 hours.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled follow-up visits for suture removal and healing checks.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Periodontal Flap Surgery
documents.overview:
Periodontal Flap Surgery
 
Purpose: Lifting the gums to clean the roots of teeth and repair bone damage caused by gum disease.
First 24 Hours:
- Keep the surgical dressing in place if provided.
- Avoid rinsing, spitting, or using a straw.
- Rest with your head elevated.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild discomfort and swelling are expected.
- Take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the face for 20 minutes on/off during the first 6–8 hours.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or pink saliva is normal for 1–2 days.
- Apply gentle pressure with gauze if bleeding increases.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing the surgical site until cleared by your dentist.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinse as directed.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for several days.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or spicy foods.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may dissolve or require removal in 1–2 weeks.
- Contact the office if swelling worsens, pain increases, or bleeding persists beyond 48 hours.

documents.name: Periodontal Regenerative Surgery
documents.overview:
Periodontal Regenerative Surgery
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure to restore lost bone and tissue around teeth using grafts, membranes, or biologic
agents.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics as directed.
- Mild tooth sensitivity to temperature and pressure may last for several weeks.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the surgical site until instructed.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial mouth rinses to maintain cleanliness.
Diet:
- Stick to soft foods for 3–5 days.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or sticky foods that can disturb the healing area.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid strenuous activities for the first 48 hours.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled follow-up visits to monitor tissue and bone regeneration.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Porcelain Veneers
documents.overview:
Porcelain Veneers
 
Purpose: Thin shells of porcelain bonded to the front surfaces of teeth to improve appearance.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing until numbness wears off.
- Temporary veneers require extra care; avoid sticky, hard, or highly pigmented foods until permanent veneers
are placed.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild gum soreness or temperature sensitivity is normal.
- Use OTC pain relievers as needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, being gentle around temporary veneers.
- Avoid abrasive toothpaste that could scratch veneers.
Diet:
- Avoid very hard foods (ice, nuts, hard candy) to prevent chipping.
- Limit consumption of staining foods and beverages (coffee, tea, red wine).
Special Precautions:
- Do not use teeth as tools to open packages or bite hard objects.
- Wear a nightguard if recommended to prevent damage from grinding.
Follow-Up:
- Veneers should feel comfortable and natural.
- Contact the office if a veneer chips, cracks, or feels loose.

documents.name: Pulpotomy (1)
documents.overview:
Pulpotomy (Primary or Permanent Teeth)
 
Purpose: Removal of the diseased portion of the dental pulp (nerve tissue) within the crown of the tooth,
preserving the remaining healthy pulp tissue.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild discomfort is normal after anesthesia wears off.
- Avoid chewing on the treated tooth until numbness subsides.
- Some sensitivity to temperature may occur.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- OTC pain relievers may be used as directed.
- Avoid extreme hot or cold foods for a few days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, being gentle around the treated tooth.
- Maintain good oral hygiene to prevent further decay.
Diet:
- Soft diet for the first day; gradually return to normal eating.
- Avoid sticky, hard, or chewy foods that could dislodge temporary fillings.
Special Precautions:
- A crown or final restoration may be required; avoid biting hard foods until it is placed.
- Monitor for signs of swelling, pain, or sensitivity that worsens.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up visits for permanent restoration placement if needed.
- Contact the office if there is persistent pain, swelling, or signs of infection.

documents.name: Pulpotomy
documents.overview:
Pulpotomy
 
Purpose: Removal of the infected or inflamed pulp tissue from the crown portion of a tooth, often in children, to
preserve the remaining healthy pulp.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing on the treated tooth until numbness wears off.
- Some tenderness or mild discomfort is normal.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC or prescribed pain relievers as directed.
- Tooth sensitivity to temperature or pressure may last for several days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, avoiding excessive pressure on the treated tooth.
Diet:
- Soft foods are recommended for the first day.
- Avoid sticky or hard foods that could dislodge temporary fillings.
Special Precautions:
- If a stainless steel crown or temporary restoration is placed, avoid chewing gum or sticky candies.
Follow-Up:
- A permanent restoration may be required later.
- Contact the office if pain worsens, swelling occurs, or the restoration becomes loose.

documents.name: Ridge Augmentation
documents.overview:
Ridge Augmentation
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure to rebuild or increase the height and width of the jawbone ridge, often to prepare for
dental implants.
First 24–72 Hours:
- Swelling, bruising, and mild bleeding are common.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain relievers and antibiotics as directed.
- Some numbness in the area may occur temporarily.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth carefully, avoiding the surgical site.
- Begin gentle antimicrobial or warm salt water rinses 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Soft foods for at least one week.
- Avoid chewing on the surgical side and stay away from hard or crunchy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol during healing.
- Avoid disturbing the site with your tongue or fingers.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up visits to check bone graft stability and healing progress.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection appear.

documents.name: Ridge Preservation After Extraction
documents.overview:
Ridge Preservation After Extraction
 
Purpose: Bone graft material placed into the extraction site to maintain bone for future implants.
First 24 Hours:
- Follow the same instructions as a simple extraction.
- Do not disturb the graft site by touching it with your tongue or fingers.
- Avoid swishing, spitting, or using a straw.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild swelling and discomfort are normal.
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs 20 minutes on/off for the first day.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or pink saliva is normal for 24–48 hours.
- If bleeding increases, apply firm pressure with gauze for 30 minutes.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the graft site for 1 week.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinse as directed.
- Brush remaining teeth normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first 3–4 days.
- Avoid seeds, nuts, chips, or foods that can get into the graft site.
Follow-Up:
- Contact the office if you see continuous loss of graft material after the first week.
- Healing will be evaluated at follow-up; implants are typically placed 3–6 months later.

documents.name: Root Amputation
documents.overview:
Root Amputation
 
Purpose: Surgical removal of one root of a multi-rooted tooth while preserving the remaining tooth structure, often
to treat localized infection or damage.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are expected.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the cheek for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Mild sensitivity in the treated tooth is normal for several days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the surgical site for the first few days.
- Begin gentle warm salt water rinses 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first 48 hours.
- Avoid chewing on the treated side until your dentist advises otherwise.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid smoking and alcohol during healing.
- Do not disturb the surgical site with your tongue or fingers.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up visits to monitor healing and tooth stability.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Root Canal Therapy
documents.overview:
Root Canal Therapy
 
Purpose: Removal of infected or damaged pulp tissue from inside the tooth, followed by sealing.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing on the treated tooth until numbness wears off.
- Some tenderness or mild discomfort is normal.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC or prescribed pain relievers as directed.
- Tooth sensitivity to pressure may last for several days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, avoiding excessive pressure on the treated tooth.
Diet:
- Soft foods are recommended until chewing comfort improves.
Special Precautions:
- If a temporary filling is placed, avoid sticky or hard foods until the permanent restoration is done.
Follow-Up:
- A crown or permanent filling is usually required for full protection.
- Contact the office if pain worsens, swelling develops, or you notice signs of infection.

documents.name: Scaling and Root Planing (1)
documents.overview:
Scaling and Root Planing (Deep Cleaning)
 
Purpose: Non-surgical periodontal therapy to remove plaque, tartar, and bacteria from below the gumline and
smooth root surfaces to promote healing.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild gum soreness and slight bleeding are normal.
- Increased tooth sensitivity to temperature or sweets may occur temporarily.
- Avoid extremely hot or spicy foods.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers if necessary.
- Sensitivity toothpaste can help reduce discomfort.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush twice daily with a soft-bristled toothbrush.
- Floss daily, being gentle around treated areas.
- Use an antimicrobial mouth rinse if prescribed.
Diet:
- Soft diet for the first day to minimize irritation.
- Avoid alcohol-containing beverages or rinses during healing.
Special Precautions:
- Do not smoke for at least 48 hours, as it can delay healing.
- If localized antibiotic therapy was placed, follow special instructions given by your provider.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled periodontal maintenance appointments every 3–4 months.
- Contact the office if swelling, persistent bleeding, or severe pain develops.

documents.name: Scaling and Root Planing
documents.overview:
Scaling and Root Planing (Deep Cleaning)
 
Purpose: Removal of plaque and tartar from below the gumline to treat gum disease.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild tooth sensitivity and gum soreness are common.
- Avoid eating until numbness wears off to prevent injury.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers as needed.
- Tooth sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweets may last for several weeks.
- Desensitizing toothpaste may help.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush gently but thoroughly twice daily.
- Floss carefully to avoid injuring the gums.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinse if provided.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first day if gums are sore.
- Avoid sticky, hard, or crunchy foods until comfortable.
Bleeding:
- Mild gum bleeding during brushing or flossing is normal for several days.
- Continue good oral hygiene to promote healing.
Follow-Up:
- Schedule maintenance cleanings every 3–4 months.
- Contact the office if swelling, severe pain, or heavy bleeding occurs.

documents.name: Sinus Augmentation
documents.overview:
Sinus Augmentation (Sinus Lift)
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure to add bone to the upper jaw in the area of the molars and premolars, lifting the
sinus membrane to make room for bone grafting, often in preparation for implants.
First 24–72 Hours:
- Swelling, bruising, and mild bleeding from the nose or mouth are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the cheek area for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep your head elevated when resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics as directed.
- Avoid blowing your nose or sneezing forcefully to protect the graft site.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth gently, avoiding the surgical area.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to keep the mouth clean.
Diet:
- Soft foods for at least one week.
- Avoid using straws or creating suction in the mouth.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid bending over or heavy lifting for the first week.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled visits to monitor graft integration and sinus health.
- Contact your dentist if swelling worsens after 3 days, there is excessive nasal bleeding, or signs of infection
develop.

documents.name: Sinus Lift Augmentation
documents.overview:
Sinus Lift / Sinus Augmentation
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure to increase bone height in the upper jaw by lifting the sinus membrane and placing
bone graft material, typically for future implant placement.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild swelling, bleeding, and nasal stuffiness are normal.
- Avoid blowing your nose for at least 7–10 days to prevent pressure on the surgical site.
- Apply an ice pack externally in 15-minute intervals to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Some sinus pressure or mild headache is normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth carefully, avoiding the surgical site.
- Rinse gently with warm salt water starting 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for at least the first week.
- Avoid very hot, spicy, or crunchy foods that could irritate the area.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid using straws, smoking, or any activity that creates suction in the mouth.
- If you sneeze, do so with your mouth open to reduce sinus pressure.
- Take prescribed antibiotics and decongestants as directed.
Follow-Up:
- Sutures may dissolve on their own or require removal.
- Contact the office if you experience excessive bleeding, persistent nasal discharge, severe pain, or swelling that
worsens after 3 days.

documents.name: Sinus Lift Surgery
documents.overview:
Sinus Lift Surgery
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure to add bone below the sinus for future implant placement.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid blowing your nose or sneezing with your mouth closed to protect the surgical area.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
- Do not rinse, spit, or use a straw.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild swelling and discomfort are expected.
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the cheek for 20 minutes on/off for the first 6–8 hours.
Bleeding:
- Light bleeding from the nose or mouth is normal for 1–2 days.
- Apply gentle pressure with gauze if oral bleeding increases.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the surgical site for several days.
- Use antimicrobial rinse if prescribed.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft foods for at least 1 week.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or sticky foods that may disturb the site.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid air travel, swimming, or scuba diving for at least 2 weeks, or as directed.
- If you must sneeze, do so with your mouth open.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may be removed in 1–2 weeks.
- Contact the office if you experience nasal discharge of graft material, severe pain, or swelling after day 3.

documents.name: Sinus Perforation Repair
documents.overview:
Sinus Perforation Repair
 
Purpose: A surgical procedure to repair an opening between the mouth and the sinus cavity, often caused by
tooth extraction or trauma.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding, nasal congestion, and facial swelling are common.
- Apply ice packs to the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep your head elevated when resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics as directed.
- Avoid blowing your nose for at least 10–14 days to prevent disrupting the repair.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the surgical area for the first week.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to keep the mouth clean.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for the first week.
- Avoid hot, spicy, crunchy, or sticky foods.
Special Precautions:
- Do not use straws, sneeze with your mouth closed, or create suction in the mouth.
- Avoid smoking and alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend all follow-up appointments to check healing progress.
- Contact your dentist if you experience persistent nasal leakage, worsening swelling, or signs of infection.

documents.name: Sleep Apnea Appliance
documents.overview:
Sleep Apnea Appliance Delivery
 
Purpose: Custom oral appliance designed to reposition the jaw or tongue to maintain an open airway during
sleep.
First 24 Hours:
- Wear the appliance as instructed, typically every night.
- Some mild soreness or tightness in teeth and jaw is normal initially.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed.
- Perform any jaw stretching exercises recommended by your dentist.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss teeth before inserting the appliance.
- Clean the appliance daily with a toothbrush and mild soap or appliance cleaner.
- Avoid hot water to prevent warping.
Diet:
- Do not eat or drink (except water) while wearing the appliance.
Special Precautions:
- Store the appliance in its protective case when not in use.
- Keep away from pets, as they may chew on it.
Follow-Up:
- Bring the appliance to check-ups for evaluation and adjustment.
- Contact the office if discomfort persists, the appliance feels loose, or breathing issues return.

documents.name: Socket Preservation
documents.overview:
Socket Preservation (Ridge Preservation)
 
Purpose: Procedure performed after tooth extraction to preserve the bone and gum tissue for future implant
placement.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the cheek for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep your head elevated when resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Mild tenderness at the surgical site is normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing directly over the site for the first few days.
- Rinse gently with warm salt water starting 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the first 48 hours.
- Avoid chewing on the treated side and avoid spicy, acidic, or hard foods.
Special Precautions:
- Do not disturb the site or remove any protective dressing.
- Avoid smoking and alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up appointments to check healing and bone preservation.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Soft Tissue Graft
documents.overview:
Soft Tissue Graft
 
Purpose: Transplanting gum tissue to cover exposed roots, thicken thin gums, or improve aesthetics.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid pulling on your lip to view the surgical site.
- Do not rinse, spit, or use a straw.
- Keep head elevated when resting.
Pain & Swelling:
- Mild discomfort is normal; take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the face for 20 minutes on/off for the first 6–8 hours.
Bleeding:
- Slight bleeding or oozing is normal for the first 24–48 hours.
- Apply gentle pressure with moist gauze if needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Do not brush or floss the graft site until cleared by your dentist.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial mouth rinse as directed.
- Brush and floss other areas normally.
Diet:
- Soft, cool foods for 1–2 weeks.
- Avoid spicy, crunchy, or hot foods that could irritate the graft.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid strenuous activity for 48 hours.
- Do not smoke, as it delays healing.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may dissolve or require removal in 1–2 weeks.
- Contact the office if the graft appears loose, there is excessive bleeding, or pain increases after day 3.

documents.name: Soft Tissue Grafting
documents.overview:
Soft Tissue Grafting (Connective Tissue Graft, Free Gingival Graft)
Purpose: Surgical procedure to replace or augment gum tissue, often to cover exposed roots or increase tissue
thickness.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Apply ice packs externally in 15-minute intervals to control swelling.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Expect some tenderness at both the graft site and donor site.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss other areas normally, but avoid the graft and donor sites until advised.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses as directed.
- Do not disturb the sutures or graft material.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first week.
- Avoid hot, spicy, acidic, or crunchy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Do not pull on lips or cheeks to look at the graft.
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they slow healing.
- Protect the graft area from trauma during chewing.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may dissolve or require removal depending on type.
- Contact the office if graft tissue becomes loose, excessive bleeding occurs, or there are signs of infection.

documents.name: Surgical Exposure Impacted Teeth
documents.overview:
Surgical Exposure of Impacted Teeth (for Orthodontic Bonding)
Purpose: Surgical uncovering of an impacted tooth, often followed by bonding of an orthodontic bracket to help
guide the tooth into place.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild bleeding and swelling are normal.
- Apply ice packs externally in 15-minute intervals to control swelling.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Some soreness and jaw stiffness are normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush gently around the surgical site with a soft-bristled toothbrush.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to maintain cleanliness.
Diet:
- Eat soft, cool foods for the first few days.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or sticky foods that could dislodge the bracket or irritate the site.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid pulling on lips or cheeks to inspect the surgical area.
- Follow all orthodontist instructions regarding elastics or traction devices attached to the bracket.
Follow-Up:
- Sutures may dissolve or require removal.
- Contact the office if the bracket comes off, excessive bleeding occurs, or there are signs of infection.

documents.name: Surgical Extraction Cysts Benign Lesions
documents.overview:
Surgical Extraction of Cysts or Benign Lesions
 
Purpose: Removal of cysts or benign growths from the jawbone or soft tissues to prevent damage, infection, or
distortion of normal structures.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Swelling and mild discomfort are common.
- Apply ice packs to the surgical area for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first 24 hours.
- Keep head elevated when resting to minimize swelling.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain relievers and antibiotics as directed.
- Some bruising may occur in the surrounding tissues.
Oral Hygiene:
- Gently brush teeth away from the surgical site.
- Begin warm salt water rinses after 24 hours to aid healing.
Diet:
- Soft diet for the first few days.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or spicy foods that may irritate the site.
Special Precautions:
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol during the healing period.
- Avoid touching or disturbing the surgical site.
- Follow instructions for any drains or packing material placed.
Follow-Up:
- Stitches may be dissolvable or require removal.
- Contact the office if there is increased pain, swelling after 3 days, pus drainage, or fever.

documents.name: Surgical Orthodontics
documents.overview:
Surgical Orthodontics (Jaw Surgery)
 
Purpose: Corrective jaw surgery to realign the jaws, improve bite function, and enhance facial balance, often in
conjunction with orthodontic treatment.
First 24–72 Hours:
- Significant swelling and bruising are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the face for the first 24 hours, then switch to warm compresses to reduce swelling.
- Keep head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain relievers and antibiotics as directed.
- Numbness in lips, cheeks, or chin may occur and can last several weeks.
Oral Hygiene:
- Follow your surgeon’s instructions for cleaning the mouth; often includes gentle rinsing with antimicrobial
solution.
- Avoid brushing near surgical sites until cleared.
Diet:
- Liquid or pureed diet initially, transitioning to soft foods as directed.
- Avoid chewing until your surgeon advises it is safe.
Special Precautions:
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol during recovery.
- Avoid strenuous activity until cleared by your surgeon.
- Elastic bands or wires may be in place—do not remove unless instructed.
Follow-Up:
- Multiple follow-up visits will be required to monitor healing and adjust orthodontic appliances.
- Contact your surgeon if you experience persistent bleeding, difficulty breathing, severe pain, or signs of
infection.

documents.name: Surgical Removal Supernumerary Teeth
documents.overview:
Surgical Removal of Supernumerary Teeth
 
Purpose: Surgical extraction of extra teeth (supernumerary teeth) that can cause crowding, delayed eruption, or
other dental problems.
First 24 Hours:
- Mild swelling and bleeding are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time to reduce swelling.
- Keep the head elevated when resting.
- Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using straws for the first 24 hours.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Some soreness in the gums and jaw is expected.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth gently, avoiding the surgical site.
- Begin warm salt water rinses after 24 hours, several times daily.
Diet:
- Soft foods are recommended for the first few days.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or sticky foods that may disrupt healing.
Special Precautions:
- Do not smoke or consume alcohol while healing.
- Avoid touching the extraction site with fingers or tongue.
- Stitches may be placed and will either dissolve or require removal.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled post-op appointments to monitor healing.
- Contact the office if bleeding persists, swelling worsens after 3 days, or signs of infection develop.

documents.name: Surgical Tooth Extraction
documents.overview:
Surgical Tooth Extraction
 
Purpose: Removal of a tooth requiring gum incision and/or bone removal.
First 24 Hours:
- Follow the same bleeding control instructions as a simple extraction.
- Expect more swelling and soreness compared to a simple extraction.
- Keep head elevated when resting.
Pain & Swelling:
- Take prescribed or OTC pain relievers as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the cheek for 20 minutes on/off for the first 6–8 hours.
- Swelling may peak at 48–72 hours.
- Switch to warm compresses after 48 hours if swelling remains.
Bleeding:
- Light oozing is normal; replace gauze and bite firmly for 30 minutes if needed.
- A moistened tea bag can promote clotting.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid rinsing for the first 24 hours.
- After 24 hours, gently rinse with warm salt water 3–4 times a day.
- Brush carefully, avoiding the surgical site.
Diet:
- Soft foods for 2–3 days.
- Avoid small seeds or grains that may enter the socket.
Activity:
- Rest for at least 24 hours.
- Avoid strenuous activity for several days.
Follow-Up:
- Return for suture removal if placed.
- Call if pain or swelling worsens, or if bleeding persists beyond the first day.

documents.name: TAD Placement
documents.overview:
TAD (Temporary Anchorage Device) Placement in Orthodontics
Purpose: Placement of a small screw-like device in the jawbone to provide stable anchorage for orthodontic tooth
movement.
