First 24 Hours:
- Mild soreness and swelling are normal.
- Avoid touching the TAD with your fingers or tongue.
- Do not use the area for chewing.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed.
- Mild discomfort is common for the first 1–2 days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush normally but avoid the immediate area around the TAD for the first 24 hours.
- Use an antimicrobial mouth rinse as directed to keep the site clean.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for the first day.
- Avoid sticky, hard, or crunchy foods that may dislodge the TAD.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid playing with or pushing on the TAD with your tongue.
- Do not attempt to tighten or adjust the device yourself.
- Avoid contact sports unless using a mouthguard.
Follow-Up:
- The orthodontist will check stability and cleanliness at regular visits.
- Contact the office if the TAD feels loose, causes significant pain, or there are signs of infection.

documents.name: TMJ Arthrocentesis Arthroscopy
documents.overview:
TMJ Arthrocentesis / Arthroscopy
 
Purpose: Minimally invasive procedures used to diagnose or treat temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders,
relieve pain, and improve jaw function.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Swelling and mild discomfort are common.
- Apply ice packs to the area in 15–20 minute intervals for the first 24 hours.
- Keep your head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications or anti-inflammatory drugs as directed.
- Mild jaw stiffness is normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush teeth normally but avoid excessive jaw movement.
- Use antimicrobial rinse if prescribed.
Diet:
- Soft diet for the first few days.
- Avoid chewing gum, hard, or chewy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Limit jaw opening as advised by your provider.
- Perform any prescribed jaw exercises as directed to maintain mobility.
- Avoid strenuous activity for at least 48 hours.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up visits for evaluation and additional treatment if needed.
- Contact the office if you experience severe pain, difficulty opening the mouth, fever, or signs of infection.

documents.name: TMJ Surgery
documents.overview:
TMJ Surgery
 
Purpose: Surgical treatment for temporomandibular joint disorders to improve jaw function, reduce pain, and
correct structural problems.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Swelling, stiffness, and discomfort are normal.
- Apply ice packs to the side of the face for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep head elevated to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and anti-inflammatory drugs as directed.
- Mild ear pain or clicking sounds may occur temporarily.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush gently, avoiding excessive jaw movement.
- Use antimicrobial rinses if prescribed.
Diet:
- Soft or liquid diet for the first week to avoid stress on the joint.
- Avoid chewy, hard, or crunchy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid wide mouth opening, yawning, or chewing gum during recovery.
- Perform gentle jaw exercises only if instructed by your surgeon.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled visits to monitor joint healing and function.
- Contact your surgeon if you experience worsening pain, inability to open or close your mouth, or signs of
infection.

documents.name: TMJ Therapy
documents.overview:
TMJ Therapy (Splints, Exercises, etc.)
 
Purpose: Treatment for temporomandibular joint disorders to reduce pain, improve jaw function, and prevent
further damage.
First 24 Hours:
- Follow appliance wear instructions exactly (daytime, nighttime, or both).
- Use ice packs externally for 15-minute intervals to reduce swelling if discomfort occurs.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild soreness or tightness in jaw muscles may occur initially.
- Use OTC pain relievers as directed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Clean any appliances daily with a toothbrush and mild soap or appliance cleaner.
- Brush teeth and floss normally.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods during initial treatment to reduce strain on the jaw.
- Avoid chewing gum, hard foods, and very chewy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid wide mouth opening (yawning excessively, biting large sandwiches).
- Perform any prescribed jaw exercises as instructed.
Follow-Up:
- Bring the appliance to every appointment for evaluation and adjustment.
- Contact the office if pain increases, jaw locking occurs, or the appliance is damaged.

documents.name: Tooth Colored Fillings
documents.overview:
Tooth-Colored Fillings (Composite Restorations)
 
Purpose: Restoration of decayed or damaged teeth using composite resin for a natural appearance.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing until numbness wears off.
- Composite fillings harden immediately, but chewing may cause discomfort initially.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Mild sensitivity to pressure, temperature, or sweets may occur for a few days.
- Use OTC pain relievers if needed.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, taking care around the filled tooth.
Diet:
- Avoid very hard or sticky foods for the rest of the day.
- Resume normal diet as comfort allows.
Special Precautions:
- If your bite feels uneven after numbness wears off, contact the office for adjustment.
Follow-Up:
- Sensitivity should gradually decrease.
- Contact the office if pain worsens or persists beyond a week.

documents.name: Tooth Whitening
documents.overview:
Tooth Whitening (In-Office and Take-Home)
 
Purpose: Cosmetic procedure to lighten and brighten teeth using bleaching agents.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid consuming staining foods or drinks (coffee, tea, red wine, berries, dark sauces).
- Do not smoke or use tobacco products.
Sensitivity:
- Temporary tooth sensitivity is common, especially to cold.
- Use sensitivity toothpaste if needed.
- Avoid very hot or cold foods for 1–2 days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss gently using a soft-bristled toothbrush.
- Continue using desensitizing toothpaste for a few days if needed.
Diet:
- Stick to “white” or light-colored foods for the first 24–48 hours.
- Avoid acidic foods that may increase sensitivity.
Special Precautions:
- Follow provided instructions for take-home kits carefully.
- Do not overuse whitening products, as this can cause enamel damage.
Follow-Up:
- Sensitivity should resolve within a few days.
- Touch-up treatments may be recommended periodically to maintain results.

documents.name: Tori Removal
documents.overview:
Tori Removal
 
Purpose: Surgical removal of excess bony growths (tori) in the mouth, typically to improve comfort, function, or to
facilitate denture placement.
First 24–48 Hours:
- Bleeding, swelling, and discomfort are normal.
- Apply ice packs for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first day.
- Keep your head elevated while resting.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics as directed.
- Mild tenderness and difficulty chewing are normal for several days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing near the surgical site for the first week.
- Use prescribed antimicrobial rinses to maintain cleanliness.
Diet:
- Eat soft foods for the first week.
- Avoid hard, crunchy, or spicy foods.
Special Precautions:
- Avoid vigorous rinsing or spitting for 48 hours.
- Do not smoke or drink alcohol during healing.
Follow-Up:
- Attend follow-up visits for suture removal and healing checks.
- Contact your dentist if heavy bleeding occurs, swelling worsens after 3 days, or you notice signs of infection.

documents.name: Vestibuloplasty (1)
documents.overview:
Vestibuloplasty
 
Purpose: Surgical procedure to deepen the oral vestibule (space between the lips/cheeks and gums) to improve
denture stability or oral function.
First 24–72 Hours:
- Swelling, mild bleeding, and discomfort are common.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of the mouth for 15–20 minutes at a time during the first 24 hours.
- Keep head elevated to reduce swelling.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Take prescribed pain medications and antibiotics exactly as directed.
- Mild tightness or stretching sensation in the lips/cheeks is normal.
Oral Hygiene:
- Avoid brushing near the surgical site until cleared by your dentist.
- Rinse gently with antimicrobial mouthwash or warm salt water starting 24 hours after surgery.
Diet:
- Soft or liquid diet for the first few days.
- Avoid hot, spicy, and crunchy foods until fully healed.
Special Precautions:
- Do not pull on the lips or cheeks to look at the surgical site.
- Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they slow healing.
- Refrain from strenuous activity until cleared.
Follow-Up:
- Attend scheduled appointments to monitor healing.
- Contact your dentist if bleeding persists, swelling increases after 3 days, or signs of infection occur.

documents.name: Vital Pulp Therapy
documents.overview:
Vital Pulp Therapy (Direct Pulp Capping)
 
Purpose: Treatment to protect the dental pulp after it has been exposed due to decay or trauma, aiming to
preserve its vitality.
First 24 Hours:
- Avoid chewing on the treated tooth until numbness wears off.
- Mild sensitivity is normal.
Pain & Sensitivity:
- Use OTC pain relievers as needed.
- Sensitivity to temperature or pressure may last for a few days.
Oral Hygiene:
- Brush and floss normally, being gentle around the treated tooth.
Diet:
- Soft foods for the rest of the day.
- Avoid sticky or hard foods until permanent restoration is placed.
Special Precautions:
- If a temporary filling is used, be cautious to avoid dislodging it.
Follow-Up:
- A permanent restoration (filling or crown) may be needed.
- Contact the office if pain increases, swelling develops, or the filling becomes loose.

documents.name: Wisdom Tooth Removal
documents.overview:
Wisdom Tooth Removal
 
Purpose: Removal of impacted or partially erupted third molars.
First 24 Hours:
- Same bleeding and clot care as other extractions.
- Expect facial swelling, jaw stiffness, and possible bruising.
Pain & Swelling:
- Take prescribed pain medication as directed.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of your face for 20 minutes on/off for the first 24 hours.
- Switch to warm compresses after 48 hours to help with stiffness.
- Gentle jaw stretching after 3 days can help prevent limited opening.
Diet:
- Liquid and soft foods for 3–5 days.
- Avoid straws for 1 week to prevent dislodging the clot.
Activity:
- Rest for 2–3 days after surgery.
- Avoid sports or activities that may cause trauma to the face.
Special Precautions:
- If upper wisdom teeth were removed near the sinuses, avoid blowing your nose for 1 week.
- Sneeze with your mouth open to avoid pressure in the sinus.
Follow-Up:
- Suture removal if required.
- Contact the office if you experience persistent numbness, fever, foul taste, or swelling that worsens after 3 days.

documents.name: I.V. Sedation
documents.overview:
Purpose: Provide safe, comfortable dental treatment using intravenous sedation while maintaining proper breathing and response.
First 24 Hours:
- A responsible adult should remain with you today and overnight.
- No driving, operating machinery, alcohol, recreational drugs, or signing legal documents until tomorrow.
- Expect drowsiness, lightheadedness, or mild forgetfulness—move slowly from lying to standing.
- Sleep with your head elevated; use CPAP/BiPAP if prescribed.
Pain & Swelling:
- Begin prescribed/approved pain medication before numbness fully wears off.
- If permitted, many patients alternate ibuprofen and acetaminophen; follow label limits.
- Apply ice packs to the outside of your face for 20 minutes on/off for the first 24 hours.
- Switch to warm compresses after 48 hours to help with stiffness.
- Gentle jaw stretching after 3 days can help prevent limited opening if your jaw is sore.
Diet:
- Start with clear liquids (water, electrolyte drinks, broth), then advance to soft foods (yogurt, eggs, mashed potatoes).
- Avoid hot foods/drinks until numbness is gone to prevent burns.
- If you had extractions or grafting, avoid straws for at least 1 week to protect the blood clot.
Activity:
- Rest the day of your procedure; light activity the next day as tolerated.
- Avoid strenuous exercise, heavy lifting, or bending over for 48 hours.
- Change positions slowly to reduce dizziness or fainting.
Special Precautions:
- Take only medications listed on your after-visit summary or prescriptions; do not mix with extra sedatives.
- Nausea can occur—use small sips of clear fluids; take the prescribed anti-nausea medicine if needed.
- Patients with diabetes should monitor glucose more often today and maintain hydration.
- Breastfeeding: confirm medication compatibility before nursing; you may be advised to pump and discard breast milk.
- Call if you have trouble breathing, bluish lips, or severe snoring that doesn't improve when repositioned.
Follow-Up:
- Contact the office for: fever over 101°F (38.3°C), heavy bleeding, worsening pain not relieved by medication.
- Use the after-hours number provided on your paperwork. If you experience severe breathing trouble or other concerning symptoms, seek immediate medical attention.

documents.instructions:
Post-Operative Instructions
 All-on-X Dental Implants with Temporary PMMA Prosthesis
Bleeding
Some minor oozing is normal for the first 24–48 hours. Bite gently on gauze packs placed after surgery.
Replace them every 30–45 minutes as needed until bleeding slows. If bleeding persists, bite gently on
a moistened tea bag for 30 minutes. Avoid spitting, rinsing forcefully, or using straws, as this can
dislodge the clot.
Swelling & Bruising
Swelling is common and may peak at 48–72 hours. Apply an ice pack (20 minutes on, 20 minutes off)
during the first 24 hours. Keep your head elevated when resting. Bruising may appear and is normal—it
should fade in a week or so.
Pain Control
Take prescribed medications as directed. Over-the-counter pain relievers (ibuprofen, acetaminophen)
may be used if advised by your dentist. Do not drive or operate machinery while taking narcotic pain
medication.
Diet
For the first 6–8 weeks, follow a soft diet only. This allows the implants to heal without unnecessary
stress. Examples: yogurt, scrambled eggs, mashed potatoes, smoothies, pasta, well-cooked
vegetables, fish. Avoid hard, crunchy, or sticky foods (nuts, chips, raw carrots, tough meats). Do not
bite directly into food with your front teeth—cut food into small pieces.
Oral Hygiene
Do not brush directly on the surgical sites for the first week. After 24 hours, gently rinse with warm salt
water (½ teaspoon salt in 8 oz warm water) 3–4 times daily. Use any prescribed antimicrobial rinse
(e.g., chlorhexidine) as directed. After 7–10 days, you may begin gently brushing the prosthesis with a
soft toothbrush. Avoid vigorous scrubbing. Do not use water flossers or electric toothbrushes near the
surgical area until cleared by your dentist.
Temporary Prosthesis Care
Your PMMA prosthesis is temporary and designed to protect the implants during healing. Do not try to
remove it yourself—it has been secured by your dentist. Some speech changes and increased saliva
are normal and will improve with time. Minor pressure points may occur; call us if you notice sore spots.
Activity

Rest and avoid strenuous exercise for the first 48–72 hours. Gradually return to normal activity as you
feel comfortable. Avoid smoking and alcohol, as they delay healing and increase risk of implant failure.
What to Expect
You may feel tightness or pressure under the prosthesis. This is normal. Small gaps between the gums
and prosthesis may appear as swelling decreases—these will be adjusted at follow-up visits. The
PMMA temporary will eventually be replaced with your final permanent prosthesis after the implants
have fully healed (typically 4–6 months).
Follow-Up
Attend all scheduled follow-up appointments to monitor healing and make adjustments. Call our office if
you notice: Persistent or severe bleeding, increasing pain or swelling after 3–4 days, prosthesis
loosening or breakage, or signs of infection (fever, pus, foul taste/odor).
Emergency Contact
If you have concerns outside of office hours, please call our emergency number: (insert office phone
number).

documents.instructions:
Post-Operative Instructions
 Final Zirconia Implant Prosthesis
Initial Adjustment Period
You may notice your bite feels slightly different at first. This is normal and will improve as your mouth
adapts. Speech may take a few days to fully adjust. Reading out loud can help. Increased saliva
production is also normal and will decrease as you adjust.
Comfort & Soreness
Mild soreness around the gums is common for a few days after placement. Over-the-counter pain
relievers such as ibuprofen or acetaminophen may be taken if needed. If discomfort persists or
worsens, contact our office.
Diet
You may gradually return to a normal diet, but please be cautious: Avoid chewing very hard foods (ice,
hard candy, bones, unpopped popcorn kernels) as they can fracture the zirconia or damage the
implants. Avoid extremely sticky foods (caramels, taffy, chewing gum) which can place undue stress on
the prosthesis. Cut tougher foods (steak, crusty bread, apples) into small pieces before chewing. Try to
chew evenly on both sides to distribute pressure.
Oral Hygiene
Daily cleaning is essential to the long-term health of your implants and prosthesis. Use a soft-bristled
toothbrush to gently brush the prosthesis at least twice daily. Interdental brushes (with nylon-coated
wire) or floss made for implants (such as SuperFloss or floss threaders) can help clean under the
prosthesis. A water flosser may also be used to flush food particles and plaque from beneath the
bridge—just make sure the pressure is not too high. An antimicrobial rinse (such as chlorhexidine or
alcohol-free mouthwash) may be recommended—follow your dentist’s instructions.
Prosthesis Care
Your zirconia bridge is highly durable but not indestructible. Treat it with care. Do not use your teeth as
tools (opening packages, biting fingernails, etc.). If you notice chipping, looseness, or a crack, call our
office immediately. The prosthesis is screwed into place and should only be removed by your dentist
during maintenance appointments. Do not attempt removal yourself.
Regular Maintenance
Attend all scheduled follow-up visits so your dentist can check the implants, gums, and prosthesis.
Professional cleanings every 3–6 months are recommended to remove hard-to-clean buildup around
the implants. At these visits, your dentist may remove the prosthesis to clean and inspect it.

What to Watch For
Please contact our office promptly if you notice any of the following: Pain, swelling, or bleeding around
the implants; Loosening or movement of the prosthesis; Clicking or unusual noises when chewing;
Signs of infection (bad taste, pus, foul odor, fever); Difficulty chewing that does not improve within a
week.
Lifestyle Considerations
Smoking and alcohol use can increase the risk of implant failure and should be avoided. If you grind
your teeth (bruxism), a nightguard may be recommended to protect your prosthesis. Keep your overall
health in check—conditions like diabetes and gum disease can affect implant success.
Long-Term Outlook
With proper care, your zirconia implant prosthesis can last many years. Remember: the implants and
supporting gums require just as much attention as natural teeth. Your partnership in daily home care
and regular dental checkups is critical for long-term success.
Emergency Contact
If you experience severe pain, swelling, or prosthesis breakage, please call our office immediately at
(insert office phone number). For after-hours concerns, follow the emergency instructions on our
voicemail.
